content: Adapalene is a medication prescribed for the treatment of acne. It belongs to a class of drugs known as retinoid-like compounds. Its mechanism of action involves preventing the formation of pimples beneath the skin's surface. Adapalene is available in various forms, including a gel, a liquid solution, and a cream, all of which are applied topically to the skin. The solution is provided in a glass bottle with an applicator or as single-use medicated wipes (pledgets). Typically, adapalene is applied once daily at bedtime. It is crucial to follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Use adapalene exactly as directed, without applying more or less than prescribed, as overuse will not enhance results and may irritate your skin. While adapalene helps control acne, it does not cure it. During the initial weeks of treatment, your acne may worsen, and it may take 8 to 12 weeks or longer to experience the full benefits. Pimples can take 6 to 8 weeks to form under the skin, and adapalene may bring these to the surface during the early stages of treatment. Continue using adapalene even if your acne initially worsens or if you do not see immediate improvement. Do not discontinue use without consulting your doctor. Avoid applying adapalene to sunburned, broken, or eczema-affected skin. If you have any of these conditions, wait until your skin has healed before using the medication. Take care to avoid contact with your eyes, nose, or mouth. If adapalene gets into your eyes, rinse them thoroughly with water and contact your doctor, as irritation, swelling, or infection may occur. To use the cream, gel, or solution, follow these steps: 1. Gently cleanse the affected skin with a mild soap or soap-free cleanser, then pat dry with a soft towel. Avoid harsh or abrasive cleansers and vigorous scrubbing. Consult your doctor or pharmacist for recommendations on gentle cleansers. 2. If using the gel or cream, apply a thin layer of the medication to the affected area using your fingers. If using a pledget, remove it from its foil pouch and gently wipe the entire affected area. If using the solution from a glass bottle, apply a thin layer to the affected area with the provided applicator. 3. You may experience a mild warmth or stinging sensation at the application site, which is normal and should subside shortly. 4. If using a pledget, discard it after use. Do not reuse it. Adapalene may also be prescribed for other uses. Consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Before using adapalene, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to adapalene or any other medications. Provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, nutritional supplements, and herbal products you are taking or using. Be sure to mention all skincare products, including soaps, cleansers, moisturizers, and cosmetics, as some may irritate your skin when used with adapalene. This is especially true for products that are harsh, drying, or contain alcohol, spices, lime rind, sulfur, resorcinol, salicylic acid, or alpha hydroxy acid. If you have been using such products, your doctor may advise waiting until your skin returns to normal before starting adapalene. Inform your doctor if you have or have ever had eczema or cancer. Additionally, let your doctor know if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. If you become pregnant while using adapalene, contact your doctor immediately. Avoid unnecessary or prolonged exposure to both natural and artificial sunlight, and protect your skin by wearing protective clothing, sunglasses, and sunscreen with an SPF of 15 or higher, especially if you are prone to sunburn. Also, avoid prolonged exposure to extreme cold or wind, as adapalene may increase your skin's sensitivity to sunlight and weather conditions. Do not use hot wax for hair removal during your treatment with adapalene. Unless otherwise directed by your doctor, continue your normal diet. If you miss a dose, apply it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not apply a double dose to make up for a missed one. Adapalene may cause side effects, particularly during the first 2 to 4 weeks of treatment. Common side effects include redness, scaling, dryness, burning or stinging, and itching. Inform your doctor if these symptoms are severe or persistent. Similar medications have caused tumors in laboratory animals exposed to sunlight, but it is unknown whether adapalene increases tumor risk in humans. Protect yourself from sunlight and sunlamps while using adapalene, and discuss the risks with your doctor. Report any unusual problems to your doctor. Store adapalene in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (not in the bathroom). If using a bottle of adapalene solution, store it upright. Dispose of outdated or unneeded medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. In case of accidental ingestion, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. Do not swallow adapalene, as it may lead to an overdose. Keep all appointments with your doctor. Do not share your medication with others. Consult your pharmacist if you have questions about refilling your prescription.
